questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Fills a critical DR planning gap for SAP on AWS by requiring end-to-end orchestration across SAP and AWS native services, demonstrating enterprise-level disaster recovery design capabilities.

## Key Concepts
- SAP HANA System Replication (HSR) across AWS regions with async mode for minimal data loss
- AWS Route53 health checks and failover routing policies for automated DNS management
- Cross-region EBS snapshot replication and S3 backup orchestration
- AWS Step Functions with Lambda for automated failover orchestration
- IAM role-based access control following least privilege principles
- Post-failover validation including database and application health checks

## Code Example
```yaml
# Minimal CloudFormation snippet for cross-region DR orchestration infrastructure
Resources:
  DROrchestrationRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: "2012-10-17"
        Statement:
        - Effect: Allow
          Principal:
            Service: [lambda.amazonaws.com, states.amazonaws.com]
          Action: sts:AssumeRole
      ManagedPolicyArns:
      - arn:aws:iam::aws:policy/service-role/AWSLambdaVPCAccessExecutionRole
      Policies:
      - PolicyName: DROperations
        PolicyDocument:
          Version: "2012-10-17"
          Statement:
          - Effect: Allow
            Action:
            - ec2:StartInstances
            - ec2:StopInstances
            - ec2:DescribeInstances
            - route53:ChangeResourceRecordSets
            - route53:GetHealthCheckStatus
            - s3:GetObject
            - s3:PutObject
            Resource: '*'
  Route53HealthCheck:
    Type: AWS::Route53::HealthCheck
    Properties:
      HealthCheckConfig:
        IPAddress: !Sub '${PrimaryInstanceIP}'
        Port: 80
        Type: HTTP
        ResourcePath: /health
        FailureThreshold: 2
        RequestInterval: 30
```

```yaml
AWSTemplateFormatVersion: '2010-09-09'
Resources:
  SAPRemediationRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              Service: lambda.amazonaws.com
            Action: sts:AssumeRole
      Path: '/'
      ManagedPolicyArns:
        - arn:aws:iam::aws:policy/service-role/AWSLambdaBasicExecutionRole
      Policies:
        - PolicyName: SAPRemediation
          PolicyDocument:
            Version: '2012-10-17'
            Statement:
              - Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - logs:CreateLogGroup
                  - logs:CreateLogStream
                  - logs:PutLogEvents
                Resource: '*'
              - Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - ssm:SendCommand
                Resource: '*'
  SAPRemediationFunction:
    Type: AWS::Lambda::Function
    Properties:
      Handler: index.handler
      Role: !GetAtt SAPRemediationRole.Arn
      Runtime: nodejs14.x
      Code:
        ZipFile: |
          const AWS = require('aws-sdk');
          exports.handler = async () => { console.log('Restart SAP HANA if needed'); };
  SAPHANA_CPU_Alarm:
    Type: AWS::CloudWatch::Alarm
    Properties:
      AlarmName: SAPHANA_CPU_Alarm
      MetricName: CPUUtilization
      Namespace: AWS/EC2
      Dimensions:
        - Name: InstanceId
          Value: !Ref SAPInstance
      Statistic: Average
      Period: 300
      EvaluationPeriods: 1
      Threshold: 80
      ComparisonOperator: GreaterThanOrEqualToThreshold
      AlarmActions:
        - !GetAtt SAPRemediationFunction.Arn
```
